headlines.title: Spot fires burn more than 300 acres in Marin County
headlines.description: Multiple spot fires ended up burning approximately 340 acres in Marin County on Sunday, the Marin County Fire said. The fire department said at around 4:40 p.m., crews responded to reports of a vegetation fire near Chileno Valley Road, around 4 miles south of Tomales Road, in the Chileno Valley area. Upon arrival, the fire department said it was determined there were multiple spot fires. The forward progress of one of the smaller ones was stopped at around 4:50 p.m., while the forward progress of the two remaining fires was stopped just before 7 p.m. Authorities said the spot fires burned approximately 340 acres combined.

headlines.title: Giants legend Duane Kuiper reveals throat cancer diagnosis, undergoing treatment
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Kruk and Kuip plan to call their final game together on Sept. 27, but the road to get there won’t be easy. A few weeks after Mike Krukow announced that this will be his final season, Duane Kuiper revealed Sunday that he has been diagnosed with throat cancer. Kuiper is getting treatment and will miss some upcoming games, but he plans to be in the booth next weekend with Krukow for their final series together. “I was recently diagnosed with throat cancer and began treatment last week with my doctors at Stanford Medicine,” Kuiper said in a statement released by the Giants. “This cancer is unrelated to the one I experienced five years ago, and I’m optimistic that it will be successfully treated. I’ll miss the broadcasts tomorrow and Wednesday as I continue treatment, but I’m looking forward to returning Tuesday and this weekend to celebrate my partner, Mike Krukow, and his remarkable career as he calls his final game before retirement. I’m incredibly grateful for the care I’m receiving and for the tremendous support from my family, the Giants organization, my broadcast partners and so many others.” Kuiper, 76, missed this weekend’s series against the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Jon Miller and Dave Flemming filling in. He has long planned to be back next weekend, when he and Krukow, his broadcast partner and closest friend, will call games against the Dodgers for the final time. It will be the end of a 36-year run for Krukow, who announced last month that he is retiring because his long battle with inclusion body myositis has made it difficult to continue to keep up with the physical demands of the job. Kuiper, who underwent chemotherapy in 2021, has said that he intends to keep calling games beyond this season. headlines.title: Body found in Guadalupe River Trail area in San Jose
headlines.description: A body was found in the Guadalupe River Trail area in San Jose early Sunday morning, according to the police department. Police said at around 1:15 a.m., officers responded to a report of suspicious circumstance in the area of the Guadalupe River Trail near the intersection of Coleman Avenue and Autumn Parkway. There, authorities said they found a dead person. The police department said investigation is ongoing.

headlines.title: California establishes Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day under new law
headlines.description: California has officially established Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day in honor of the renowned singer, songwriter, philanthropist and actress, the governor’s office announced Sunday. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 931, authored by State Senators Shannon Grove, R-Bakersfield, and John Laird, D-Santa Cruz. The date — 9/25 — was selected as a clever nod to Parton’s beloved hit song “9 to 5,” according to the governor’s office. “We could all afford to live a little more like Dolly. Be kind, be humble, and have some fun… Be a diamond in a rhinestone world,” Newsom said in a statement. “With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did — joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart.” Dubbed the “Queen of Country,” Parton is celebrated as one of the most successful country music performers in history, having sold more than 100 million records worldwide. Over her six-decade career, she achieved 25 number-one hits — the most by any female country artist. Her iconic anthem “I Will Always Love You” topped the charts twice, in 1974 and 1982, before Whitney Houston later covered it to enormous global acclaim. Beyond music, Parton built an enduring legacy in acting, producing, and business. Her contributions to Hollywood include her acting debut in the feminist comedy film “9 to 5,” as well as both the 1992 film and the hit television series “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” for which she served as an uncredited producer. Lawmakers emphasized that Parton’s impact stretches far beyond entertainment, particularly highlighting her humanitarian work and commitment to early childhood literacy through the Imagination Library. The program has distributed more than 300 million books to children worldwide, including across California. “Dolly Parton sparkled on every stage she ever stood on, but her brightest sparkle was the literacy legacy she built through the Imagination Library,” Grove said. “I am incredibly proud of the bipartisan work we have accomplished, from bringing her bilingual reading program statewide in California with former Senate President pro Tempore Toni Atkins, to introducing a bipartisan bill with Senator Laird to establish this annual day of remembrance.” The love Dolly gave so freely, rooted in her deep and openly shared faith, and the love the world returned to her, shows how deeply she was cherished by everyone. I thank Governor Newsom for signing SB 931 so that every September 25th, our state will remember the legend who put millions of books in the hands of our youngest readers and inspired the world on how to respect and love one another,” Grove added. Laird echoed those sentiments, noting Parton’s deep ties to the state. “I’m grateful to Governor Newsom for signing our bill and to Senator Grove for her partnership in making September 25 Dolly Parton Day in California,” Laird said in a statement. “Dolly brought joy to a lot of people, but her legacy goes well beyond her music. Through the Imagination Library, she put books into the hands of millions of children, and throughout her life she led with kindness, acceptance, and a belief that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect. She was also no stranger to the Central Coast, where she performed for packed crowds and spent time over the years. Now, every 9-2-5, California gets to celebrate Dolly and the remarkable legacy she shared with all of us,” Laird said. headlines.title: Oakland Roots reach agreement to develop Howard Terminal site
headlines.description: The Oakland Roots Soccer Club, Port of Oakland and a Southern California realty group have come to an exploratory negotiating agreement to develop the Howard Terminal site. On Sept. 10, the Port of Oakland Commissioners voted to authorize an exploratory exclusive negotiating agreement with the team, the port and Industrial Realty Group for one year at Howard Terminal, according to an agenda report. “You are probably aware that we have been playing at four different venues through our seven years existence, very nomadic,” Chief Real Estate Officer of the Oakland Roots and Soul Lydia Tan said. “I think it’s important for me personally as a commissioner to think about the opportunities at Howard as something that will provide strength and health to the entire port and all of our operations, and I think this is really good step in that direction.” A description of the respective projects, site plans, proposed acreage parking plans, potential uses, workforce and maritime integration are part of the expected timeline. in a statement, the Oakland 68s, an organization dedicated to the community and its sports culture said in part the agreement “represents an opportunity to build a new chapter for Oakland sports and the city’s waterfront.” NBC Bay Area reached out to Industrial Realty Group for comment, but hasn’t heard back yet.

headlines.title: Baby born in San Francisco traffic after family pulls over for 911 help
headlines.description: A healthy baby girl made an unexpected roadside arrival Friday afternoon after her family got stuck in heavy traffic on the way to the hospital, according to the San Francisco Fire Department. The unexpected delivery began at approximately 4:40 p.m., when crews received a report of a family en route to a hospital to deliver their baby, the department announced Saturday. Fire officials said due to heavy traffic near Crossover Drive and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, the family pulled over and called 911. SFFD Paramedic Engine 14 and AMR Unit 110, a 911 provider for San Francisco, were dispatched to the scene. AMR Unit 110 arrived first, but traffic conditions forced the crew to park two blocks away and run to reach the patient. Parents Karollyn and Nate said on Sunday a doula sitting in traffic with them helped coach Karollyn through the process while waiting for paramedics. Personnel arrived just in time to assist with the delivery of the baby girl. Engine 14 crews arrived shortly afterward to provide care for both the mother and the newborn. Both the mother and child were later transported to a local hospital and reported to be in good condition, the department stated. “We want to congratulate the family and welcome this new child to the world,” the SFFD said in a statement. “Her arrival is a true testament to the dedication, compassion and teamwork of our first responders.” On Sunday, Karollyn and Nate revealed the baby’s name is Cielle Ray. They said Karollyn is “doing great,” and she is in the recovery process. “Mom is doing great, recovering well and we’re leaving later tonight,” the family wrote. “We always joked around about giving birth in the car, never thought it would happen to us. We took a route that I take every morning to work without issues, and just so happens that the day with the worst traffic is the last day we needed it. But we were so fortunate to have the support that we did, especially some medical professionals that were sitting in the same traffic. Most notably a doula that helped coach Karollyn through the process until the paramedics arrived.

headlines.title: Bay Area students turn old tennis balls into eco-friendly tools
headlines.description: A group of local high school students in the Bay Area is serving the planet by turning old tennis balls into useful community tools. Thousands of used tennis balls are finding a new purpose at schools, animal shelters, and assisted living centers around the Bay Area, courtesy of Bin to Better, a student-led environmental organization that transforms waste into opportunity. Because the rubber and felt on a tennis ball cannot be recycled, about 125 million of them end up in landfills each year. To combat this, members of the Bin to Better organization rally on their time off, sorting through donations collected at local tennis clubs. The students cut the balls open so they can be repurposed as chair leg covers in classrooms, glides on walkers at assisted living homes and enrichment toys for pets. Fremont Elementary teacher Ms. MacKenzie notes that the modified balls work great to keep classrooms quieter while preventing scratches on the floor. The initiative is also making a splash environmentally. Kim Grant, director of the Kim Grant Tennis Academy in Palo Alto, is glad to be part of Bin to Better, saying the effort helps keep nearby waterways clean. As the organization expands and thinks outside the box for community waste solutions, founders encourage community members to ask around at local tennis clubs or check out the Bin to Better website to join the rally.

headlines.title: Alameda County health authorities alert of possible measles exposure
headlines.description: State and Bay Area health officials warned of a possible measles exposure Friday after a person infected with the disease traveled by train from the Midwest through California. Alameda County and California Department of Public health officials say an Amtrak passenger, infected with Measles, traveled from Chicago, through Sacramento, then to Emeryville, before the last leg of their journey to Los Angeles. They said that person could have infected scores of other passengers all along the way. Two frequent riders on the Sacramento to the Bay Area route just heard about the possible measles exposure on Saturday. “That is new news that I’m hearing about. It’s very worrisome,” passenger Elham A said. “It’s a risk you take in any public space. I don’t think Amtrak is particularly at fault for anything related to that. When you use public transport, if people are being silly, it can affect you,” passenger Henry N. said. According to officials, the infected passenger started their trip in Chicago on Sep. 10 and arrived in Los Angeles on Sept. 12. The passenger arrived in Bakersfield and traveled to Stockton that same day. On Sept. 13, the passenger traveled from Oroville to Sacramento, and then from Sacramento to Emeryville. On Sept. 14, the passenger left Emeryville to arrive in Denver on Tuesday. Health experts say measles cases have skyrocketed as vaccination rates have decrease; 3,400 were reported nationwide in 2026, while there were fewer than 2,300 in all of 2025. “So, we have been having the largest Measles outbreak, in since the last 35 years in this country, and now this person riding on Amtrak, actively infected with Measles, could unfortunately infect people who are not vaccinated,” UCSF Department of Medicine Dr. Monica Gandhi said. Dr. Gandhi says vaccination rates for the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine have fallen below the critical 95-percent rate across the U.S., and nine out of 10 patients hospitalized with measles are unvaccinated. “So, we really want 95% rates of vaccination, and the reason Measles is spreading in this country and we’re in this situation, is because we have people who are unvaccinated,” she said. California does still meet the 95% MMR vaccination rate, but a recent Reuters poll says only about 84% of U.S. citizens have faith in vaccines. Gandhi says there’s also a risk with vaccinated people who came into contact with the measles positive Amtrak passenger or others actively infected. She says they can still pick up and carry the disease and transmit it to others. “The concern is, you could take it home to someone who’s vulnerable, who is not vaccinated, like say a small child,” she said. The California Department of Public Health urges people to get vaccinated and to monitor for symptoms of a fever coupled with an unexplained rash. They advise anyone who believes they’ve been infected to self-isolate and call a doctor immediately. State and local health officials are working to identify and notify anyone who may have been infected.

headlines.title: Multi-vehicle crash leaves six people injured in San Francisco
headlines.description: Six people were injured following a multi-vehicle crash in San Francisco Saturday, the fire department said. The fire department said the crash occurred in the area of Park Presidio and California streets just before 7 p.m. At the scene, firefighters declared a “yellow alert multi-casualty incident,” which authorities said brings more ambulances and secures adequate emergency room occupancy for trauma patients. The fire department said all six victims were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries; three of them have moderate injuries, while three have minor injuries. Authorities warned drivers to expected delays in the area of Park Presidio Boulevard and California Street.

headlines.title: Person with an axe arrested on Cupertino college campus
headlines.description: A person was arrested on the De Anza College campus in Cupertino, the De Anza Community College District Police Department said on Friday. Police said officers on patrol noticed a person acting suspiciously on campus and made contact. Authorities said a records check revealed the person had an outstanding felony warrant. Police said officers also found the suspect had an axe, suspected methamphetamine and heroin, loaded hypodermic needles and drug paraphernalia. The person was taken into custody and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on multiple drug, weapons and warrant-related charges, according to authorities.

headlines.title: Man dies after crashing into building in Fremont
headlines.description: A man died after crashing into a building in Fremont on Saturday, according to the police department. Police said officers responded to a report of a single-vehicle crash at around 12:12 p.m. in the area of Niles Boulevard and Cinematic Common. At the scene, authorities said they found the unresponsive 88-year-old driver and provided life-saving efforts. The driver was taken to a local trauma center, where he later died, officials reported. Police said no bystanders were injured and the exact cause of the crash is under investigation, but “speed has not been ruled out”. Authorities added this is the city’s ninth fatal traffic collision in 2026.

headlines.title: UC Berkeley student says she was followed, chased into her apartment complex
headlines.description: A UC Berkeley student said she was followed and chased into her off-campus apartment building on Tuesday night. Berkeley junior Eden Winograd said this all happened at around 8 p.m. on Tuesday when she was walking her dog near her off-campus apartment complex. That night, Winograd said she was walking her dog on the same path she does every night when she noticed a man approaching whom she had seen a few days earlier. “I started to panic a little bit, but I didn’t want to offend him if he was just standing there,” she said, recalling that she then started crossing the street. But then, she said the man started following directly behind her and saying things to her while she walked. “I started speeding up and heard his feet banging on the floor behind me,” she said. “I went up to the gate, I buzzed myself in, I went, and I closed it, and then I heard clanging sounds while I was walking inside, and I turned around, and he was like scaling the gate,” Winograd continued. “My heart sank, I was out of breath, my heart was pounding,” she recalled. She made it inside the elevator of her building before anything else happened, then called the police. Winograd posted the surveillance video of the incident on TikTok, where it has now been viewed more than 858,000 times. That surveillance video has now also been shared by Berkeley Police. The video shows Winograd walking into the gate of her apartment complex, walking her dog on a leash. A few seconds later, a man can be seen climbing over the same gate where she entered and following in the same direction Winograd walked in, holding something in his hand. Police said that initial reports indicated the suspect had a knife in his hand, but investigators later found that the object was likely a barbecue lighter. It is still unclear why that man would be holding a barbecue lighter. But for Winograd, that doesn’t change how alarming this incident was. “I don’t care if they have a weapon in their hand or nothing in their hand, I don’t want to be chased the second I step out of my apartment. I don’t want to be chased and have to watch someone claw their way up a wall to get to where I live,” she said. Police said that the following day, they were called about the same man lying on the sidewalk in the same area. Berkeley police said they detained him and confirmed he was involved in “the prior trespassing incident.” Police did not arrest that man, but they did send a case to the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office for review. Police have not released the man’s name, but they said he is 50 years old and experiencing homelessness.
